history.titleZh: Modal taps Nvidia Vera CPUs after firm's internal tests show 2x throughput over Intel and AMD chips
history.descriptionZh:
Nvidia正在把AI基础设施的布局从GPU进一步扩展到CPU。据Tom's Hardware援引路透社报道，Nvidia已凭借其Vera CPU在AI云服务提供商Modal处取得一项重要设计胜利。Modal的初步评估显示，Vera在其特定工作负载上的吞吐量可达其现有AMD和Intel处理器的两倍。不过，Modal并不打算停止使用现有供应商的CPU，而是计划采用异构服务器队列，根据具体工作负载选择最合适的处理器。这一合作被视为Nvidia推动Vera成为独立服务器CPU、并在服务器市场争取更大份额的重要一步。

背景是，Nvidia依靠销售AI加速器获得了数十亿美元收入，但随着智能体AI（agentic AI）兴起，CPU在AI基础设施中的重要性明显上升。Modal提供的云基础设施使AI开发者能够部署AI智能体，这些智能体可以在较长时间内自主执行复杂操作。此类工作负载需要大量CPU资源用于软件执行、数据处理以及其他GPU难以高效完成的任务。Modal目前完全依赖AMD和Intel处理器完成这些操作，但其测试表明，Nvidia的Vera CPU可能在其特定工作负载中显著提升性能。由于Vera基于Arm指令集架构，Modal采用Vera将需要对软件进行大量修改，但Modal认为潜在的性能提升值得额外工程投入。

从技术原理看，Vera基于Arm v9.2架构的Olympus CPU核心，最多可每周期解码和执行10条指令，并配备带宽达1.2 TB/s的内存子系统。报道指出，Modal所称的两倍吞吐量优势尤其值得关注，因为智能体AI工作负载通常包含大量独立任务，这些任务会竞争CPU核心、缓存容量和内存带宽。不过，Modal尚未披露详细基准测试配置、所对比的具体AMD和Intel处理器型号，也未公布每瓦性能数据。因此，目前尚不清楚Vera的优势究竟主要来自Olympus核心的指令级并行能力、1.2 TB/s内存带宽，还是其他架构特性。此外，测试对比的是当前可用的AMD和Intel处理器，而非未来几年将与Vera竞争的下一代产品，因此这一结果不能简单等同于Vera对全部服务器CPU的普遍性能结论。

在采用策略上，Modal CEO Erik Bernhardsson表示，Modal无法在一夜之间将所有软件移植到Arm ISA，因此将继续使用AMD和Intel的x86 CPU。Modal计划运营异构服务器队列，而不是让所有工作负载统一使用一种指令集架构，并会针对每类工作负载选择最合适的处理器。未来，Modal还打算在AMD和Intel新品上市后进行评估，以决定后续选择。对Nvidia而言，这项协议是其让Vera成为独立服务器处理器并占据服务器市场重要份额的关键进展。Nvidia预计Vera在当前财年将带来至少200亿美元销售额，并估计这些CPU的潜在总可服务市场（TAM）约为2000亿美元；公司还计划在2026财年销售至少400万颗Vera CPU。

这一消息也发生在Modal完成7.5亿美元融资之后。该轮融资由Accel领投，对Modal的估值为157.5亿美元。Modal预计其年收入将在未来一年内达到10亿美元；路透社报道称，过去12个月Modal的服务消费增长了3倍，收入同比增长超过15倍。整体来看，Vera在Modal的落地展示了智能体AI时代CPU资源的重要性上升，也反映出Nvidia正试图在GPU之外建立新的服务器CPU增长曲线；但Arm软件生态迁移成本、基准测试透明度以及未来AMD/Intel产品的竞争，仍是评估Vera实际竞争力的关键变量。

history.title: Intel asks FCC for waiver to buy foreign robots
history.description: Intel is concerned that the sweeping ban on foreign-made robots means that it could not update or maintain its fleet of AGVs.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Intel has asked the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to make an exception for the automated guided vehicles (AGVs) that the company uses to transport the sensitive silicon wafers and other materials, containers, and supplies needed to make the most advanced chips in its fabs. According to Bloomberg, the American chipmaker fears that its AGVs would fall under the blanket prohibition against foreign-made robots after they were added to the FCC’s Covered List.Go deeper with TH Premium: Chipmaking (Image credit: tsmc)Analyzing TSMC's fab expansion roadmap — multi-fab N2 ramp, CoWoS, SoIC, and uncorking bottlenecksLeading-edge foundry roadmaps for TSMC, Intel, and SamsungASML's roadmap for chipmaking lithography tools examinedChinese chipmaking tool roadmaps examinedAGVs are niche machines that chip fabs use to transport materials and supplies between tools and sections of the fab, helping ensure that the cleanroom conditions required for each manufacturing process are maintained. This makes them critical equipment for U.S. semiconductor manufacturing, but, apparently, there are no suitable domestic alternatives for these devices at the moment. Intel’s current fleet of AGVs requires continuous maintenance, including software and firmware updates, and if it’s forced to find a local supplier for its AGVs, the company says that it would take years, crippling the United States’ chipmaking efforts.The biggest AGV suppliers are Japanese companies like Murata Machinery and Daifuku Co., while a few smaller businesses from South Korea and Taiwan are also trying to break into the market. It’s unclear why these companies haven’t applied for a conditional approval yet, which would allow them to continue selling these products in the U.S. while also promising Washington that they’ll set up a manufacturing base in the country. This is something that Netgear has already done, allowing it to continue selling its foreign-made routers despite being an American company.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Intel says that it remains unclear if updates to its AGVs would break compliance with the FCC, and that it’s asking the agency to issue a conditional waiver “out of an abundance of caution to ensure the ongoing operation of these specific AGV units.” While Team Blue is the only company concerned about AGVs at the moment, other chip manufacturers would likely need a similar waiver in the near future, especially as they build more fabs in the U.S. This includes TSMC, which is planning to build 12 more fabs and four packaging facilities in Arizona, Samsung, with its new Taylor, Texas, fab, and even Elon Musk’s Terafab, which has already begun construction.Washington has been using the FCC to force companies to invest in American manufacturing. Its blanket bans on foreign-made products like drones and routers have affected some of the biggest brands in the U.S., including DJI and TP-Link. While these bans do not outright ban the sale of all products made by these companies, especially those that have already been approved before, they make it impossible for them to introduce new products and even release software updates to their existing product line. The FCC eventually walked back on the software update ban, but they still would not be able to register new products unless they build them in the U.S. You may like Foreign-made robot vacuums caught up in FCC robot ban FCC proposes import ban on Chinese optical transceivers US mulling ban on key Chinese networking tech in data center component crackdown Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors

history.titleZh: 英特尔请求FCC豁免以购买外国机器人
history.descriptionZh:
英特尔已向美国联邦通信委员会（FCC）提出申请，希望为其晶圆厂内使用的自动导引车（AGV）争取有条件豁免，使其不受到FCC“覆盖清单”中对外国制造机器人禁令的影响。背景是，FCC已将外国制造机器人纳入“覆盖清单”，可能形成全面禁止进口或使用相关产品的效果。英特尔担心，其用于搬运硅晶圆、材料、容器和生产耗材的AGV会被纳入禁令范围，从而影响其最先进芯片制造业务的正常运行。

AGV是晶圆厂中的利基但关键设备，主要用于在制造工具、工段和洁净室区域之间运输敏感材料与供应品。其核心作用不仅是自动化物流，还在于减少人工介入、维持洁净室环境、降低污染风险，并保证不同制造工序所需的洁净条件。因此，AGV被视为美国半导体制造的重要基础设施。但报道指出，目前美国国内并没有合适的替代产品。英特尔现有AGV车队需要持续维护，包括软件和固件更新；如果被迫寻找本土供应商，英特尔称可能需要数年时间，这将拖累美国芯片制造能力。

从供应链看，全球最大AGV供应商包括日本村田机械和Daifuku，韩国和台湾地区的一些较小企业也在尝试进入该市场。报道未披露AGV的具体速度、负载、精度等性能参数，也未提供进口与本土设备的量化对比数据；核心对比在于替代周期和供应链成熟度：英特尔认为本土替代需要数年，而现有外国设备已深度嵌入其晶圆厂运营。报道还提到，目前不清楚这些外国供应商为何尚未申请有条件批准。该机制允许企业继续在美国销售相关产品，同时承诺在美国建立制造基地；Netgear此前已通过类似方式继续销售外国制造的路由器。

英特尔表示，目前尚不确定对AGV进行软件或固件更新是否会违反FCC合规要求，因此请求FCC“出于充分谨慎”发布有条件豁免，以确保这些特定AGV单元持续运行。虽然目前公开表达担忧的只有英特尔，但其他在美国扩产的芯片制造商未来也可能需要类似豁免。例如，台积电计划在亚利桑那州再建12座晶圆厂和4座封装设施，三星在得克萨斯州Taylor建设新晶圆厂，马斯克的Terafab也已开始建设。这些项目都将依赖大量洁净室物流自动化设备。

这一事件也反映出华盛顿正通过FCC等监管工具推动制造业回流。此前，FCC对外国制造无人机和路由器的全面限制已影响大疆、TP-Link等大型品牌。此类禁令并非一概禁止所有已获批产品的销售，但会使企业难以推出新产品，并可能影响现有产品线的软件更新。FCC后来撤回了软件更新禁令，但企业若不将生产迁至美国，仍无法注册新产品。对半导体行业而言，AGV豁免问题不仅关乎单一设备合规，还关系到先进晶圆厂扩产进度、洁净室物流自动化连续性和美国芯片制造供应链的稳定性。

history.title: Windows 98 SE users get a Thunderbolt 4 driver, thanks to AI assistance
history.description: Windows 98 devotees now have (experimental) support for USB4 and Thunderbolt 3/4. Vibe coded driver also supports Windows Me, XP, Vista, and 7.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 6 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Windows 98 SE devotees can now enjoy (experimental) support for USB4 and Thunderbolt 3/4. Developer and maker Yeo Kheng Meng, who also enjoys retrocomputing, recently released the vibe-coded xHCI98 v3.0.0.0, enabling the practical use of generic USB 3.x, USB4, and Thunderbolt 3/4 host controllers on systems running Windows 98 SE, ME, 2000, XP, Vista, and 7. An extensive blog post by the dev provides further reading about the driver, compatibility, its creation, and usage. xHCI98: xHCI host controller driver for Win 98/ME/2K/XP/Vista/7 Demo - YouTube Watch On Demo video “shows many different USB devices being hotplugged to a modern 2020 ThinkPad P14s Gen 1 with only xHCI controller.”Some of you will be wondering why a project to bring USB4 (Thunderbolt 3 and 4) to PCs running Windows 98 SE exists. Retro computing fan Meng explains on his GitHub that this project should appeal directly to users of PCs from the mid-2010s that have xHCI-only (USB 3.x) chipsets and no legacy EHCI controller. However, older OSes don’t have xHCI drivers, and that’s where xHCI98 steps in. “Without xHCI support, even keyboards, mice, and flash drives need the BIOS's legacy support, cannot be hotplugged, and devices such as Ethernet and audio do not work at all,” explains Meng, revealing his motivation. “This project fills that gap.”Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Impressively, xHCI98 drives a lot more than USB storage. It replaces Windows’ own USB port and hub drivers to facilitate the connection and use of USB 1.1 and 2.0 and SuperSpeed (USB 3.x) devices and hubs, UAS (USB Attached SCSI) storage through a second driver (xhciuas.sys), and Thunderbolt 3 and USB4 docks and NVMe enclosures through a third driver (xhcicm.sys).Meng has developed and tested xHCI98 mostly on Intel hardware, as that is what he owns. Candidly, he admits “this is a solo human's project with AI assistance, so bugs are not unexpected,” even if you do have the same hardware as the dev - a 2020 ThinkPad P14s Gen 1 (Comet Lake xHCI, no EHCI). It stands up pretty well during the plug/unplug video demo above, though the test rig used is not quite the USB cart of death. You may like Modder brings Nvidia Pascal GPU support to Windows XP 32-bit Developer uses Claude to vibe code a Windows 3.1 shell in an hour x64 port of Microsoft Word for Windows 1.1a arrives (Image credit: Yeo Kheng Meng)As a solo developer, Meng isn't shy to admit he leaned heavily on AI assistance to prepare the xHCI98 release. His vibe coding adventure was supported by Claude Fable 5.1 for planning, Claude Opus 5.5 for coding, and Codex GPT 6 Astra as an adversarial reviewer.In addition to a few bug warnings, there are some other things to know about using this driver with the various older versions of Windows it supports, standby and hibernation, and more. history.titleZh: Windows 98 SE 用户获得 Thunderbolt 4 驱动，得益于 AI 协助
history.descriptionZh:
复古计算开发者 Yeo Kheng Meng 发布了实验性的 xHCI98 v3.0.0.0 驱动，为 Windows 98 SE、ME、2000、XP、Vista 和 7 提供 xHCI 主机控制器支持，使这些老系统能够在仅配备 xHCI（USB 3.x）控制器、没有传统 EHCI 控制器的较新硬件上，实际使用通用 USB 3.x、USB4 以及 Thunderbolt 3/4 主机控制器。项目背景是：2010 年代中期以后的 PC 芯片组普遍采用 xHCI-only 设计，但旧版 Windows 不包含 xHCI 驱动，导致键盘、鼠标和闪存盘只能依赖 BIOS 的 legacy 兼容支持，无法热插拔，以太网、音频等设备甚至完全无法工作。xHCI98 正是为填补这一空白而开发。

在技术实现上，xHCI98 替代 Windows 自带的 USB 端口和 Hub 驱动，支持 USB 1.1、USB 2.0 和 SuperSpeed USB 3.x 设备及 Hub；通过第二个驱动 xhciuas.sys 支持 UAS（USB Attached SCSI）存储；通过第三个驱动 xhcicm.sys 支持 Thunderbolt 3/USB4 扩展坞和 NVMe 外置硬盘盒。开发者主要在自有的 Intel 硬件上开发和测试，典型平台为 2020 款 ThinkPad P14s Gen 1（Comet Lake xHCI，无 EHCI）。演示视频显示，多种 USB 设备可在该平台上热插拔使用。

该项目由单人开发并大量借助 AI 辅助完成，开发者坦言“这是一个人加 AI 协助的项目，出现 bug 并不意外”。其 AI 工具组合包括 Claude Fable 5.1 用于规划、Claude Opus 5.5 用于编码、Codex GPT 6 Astra 作为对抗性审查者。文章未给出量化性能基准，主要价值体现在兼容性和功能恢复：让旧操作系统重新获得现代 USB 控制器下的热插拔、存储、扩展坞和 NVMe 外设能力。该驱动目前属于实验性支持，适合复古计算、旧设备维护和特定遗留系统场景，但不应视为生产级驱动；使用前需核对硬件兼容性，并参考开发者博客中的安装、更新、待机/休眠注意事项和调优说明。

history.title: Spain-Based Startups Advance Regional Innovation With Barcelona Supercomputing Center
history.description: The Barcelona Supercomputing Center (BSC)’s AI Factory Accelerator Programme, now in full operation following a pilot initiative, gives startups access to sovereign compute, technical support and training to support innovation across industries.  Many of these companies are also members of the NVIDIA Inception program for cutting-edge startups — and as of today, access to some […]
history.content: The Barcelona Supercomputing Center (BSC)’s AI Factory Accelerator Programme, now in full operation following a pilot initiative, gives startups access to sovereign compute, technical support and training to support innovation across industries. Many of these companies are also members of the NVIDIA Inception program for cutting-edge startups — and as of today, access to some of the BSC AI Factory services are available through the NVIDIA Inception portal. NVIDIA Inception complements the BSC AI Factory Accelerator Programme by providing members with training through NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute open courses, business mentoring, venture capital connections and other resources. An upcoming extension of MareNostrum 5 — BSC’s public infrastructure serving scientific and technological innovation, powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing — will deliver supercomputing access through the BSC AI Factory and other AI Factories across Europe. BSC AI Factory is among Europe’s first AI factories and the first in Spain, and has delivered more than 800 services to private and public-sector clients since its April 2025 launch. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Three Inception members were recently named the BSC AI Factory Accelerator Programme’s AI Champions at the pilot initiative’s demo day: Qatium’s water-network platform — already used by more than 250 utilities in 16 countries — is now in early production with its Neural Water Intelligence technology, powered by proprietary AI models trained on MareNostrum 5. Built on NVIDIA accelerated computing, the NVIDIA cuGraph library, the NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo framework and NVIDIA Nemotron open models, the technology helps water utilities make better operational decisions every day. OneCareAI, a research spin-off from BSC, used NVIDIA NIM microservices to develop technology designed to identify signs of hidden atrial fibrillation — an irregular heart rhythm — in seemingly normal ECGs, helping clinicians identify patients who may be at risk of stroke before one occurs. Avatia built a voice-first, multi-agent system that provides pharmaceutical companies with agentic coworkers that support sales representatives and give doctors transparent, curated information about medicines, ultimately helping the right treatment reach the right patient sooner. The system taps into NVIDIA NIM microservices, the NVIDIA Nemotron 3 open model family and the open source NVIDIA NeMo Curator library. Other BSC AI Factory startups — Agrikola AI, Elna Health, Lokutor, Montevive AI, Oppy, Pack2Earth and Up2Smart — span precision agriculture, medical imaging and knowledge access, speech services, enterprise security, sales intelligence and sustainable packaging. The cohort reflects the breadth of what advanced intelligence can now unlock: preventing strokes, detecting breast cancer subtypes before biopsy, putting medical knowledge at doctors’ fingertips faster, replacing petroleum-based plastic with biobased compostable materials, protecting crops with robots instead of chemicals and more. history.descriptionZh:
巴塞罗那超级计算中心（BSC）的AI Factory Accelerator Programme在完成试点后已全面投入运营，为初创企业提供“主权算力”、技术支持和培训，以推动跨行业创新。该计划与NVIDIA面向前沿初创企业的Inception计划形成互补：许多BSC AI Factory成员同时也是NVIDIA Inception成员，即日起部分BSC AI Factory服务可通过NVIDIA Inception门户访问。NVIDIA Inception为成员提供NVIDIA深度学习学院公开课程、商业指导、风险投资对接等资源，从而降低初创企业使用欧洲公共超算和AI基础设施的门槛。

背景上，BSC AI Factory是欧洲首批AI工厂之一，也是西班牙首个AI工厂，自2025年4月启动以来已向私营和公共部门客户交付800多项服务。其算力基础MareNostrum 5是BSC面向科学技术创新的公共基础设施，由NVIDIA加速计算驱动；该系统的扩展将通过BSC AI Factory以及欧洲其他AI Factories提供超级计算访问能力。这意味着初创企业可以在欧洲本地公共算力底座上训练、部署和扩展AI应用，同时获得NVIDIA生态的技术与商业支持。

在试点演示日上，三家Inception成员被评为BSC AI Factory Accelerator Programme的“AI Champions”。Qatium的水网平台已被16个国家250多家公用事业公司使用，其Neural Water Intelligence技术进入早期生产阶段。该技术使用在MareNostrum 5上训练的专有AI模型，并基于NVIDIA加速计算、cuGraph图计算库、PhysicsNeMo物理与科学机器学习框架以及Nemotron开放模型，帮助水务公司改善日常运营决策。OneCareAI是BSC的研究衍生企业，利用NVIDIA NIM微服务开发技术，在看似正常的ECG中识别隐藏性心房颤动迹象，帮助临床医生在卒中发生前识别高风险患者。Avatia构建了语音优先的多智能体系统，为制药企业提供“代理同事”，支持销售代表并向医生提供透明、经过整理的信息，最终帮助正确治疗更快到达正确患者；该系统使用NVIDIA NIM微服务、Nemotron 3开放模型家族和开源NeMo Curator库。

其他BSC AI Factory初创企业包括Agrikola AI、Elna Health、Lokutor、Montevive AI、Oppy、Pack2Earth和Up2Smart，覆盖精准农业、医学影像与知识获取、语音服务、企业安全、销售智能和可持续包装等方向。这一批次体现了先进AI当前可解锁的应用广度：预防卒中、在活检前检测乳腺癌亚型、让医生更快获取医学知识、以生物基可堆肥材料替代石油基塑料、用机器人而非化学品保护作物等。整体来看，BSC AI Factory与NVIDIA Inception的衔接，将欧洲主权超算资源、NVIDIA加速计算与AI软件栈、初创培育和行业场景结合起来，形成从模型训练到微服务部署、再到行业落地的创新通道，加速AI在水务、医疗健康、制药、农业和可持续材料等领域的商业化。

history.content: CoreWeave had a bad week last week. Its bonds slipped into distressed territory by a common definition — when investors demand 1,000 basis points more in yield than they’d get from government bonds. Last Tuesday Chamath “SPAC King” Palihapitiya noticed the distressed debt, and also asked whether the AI buildout was a private credit bubble. Its shares are down more than 20 percent since Tuesday’s close, which is kind of a lot! There even seemed to be some collateral damage in the market on other AI companies, too.Now, I have also asked if the AI industry is a bubble, but when the SPAC King echoes concerns held by a lady whose ongoing question about AI is “How are we planning on affording this, champs?”, that’s a very different signal. When I say “yikes,” it’s one thing. When Elon Musk says it, that’s something else.When you talk about wanting to tap into the enormous sums of money that insurers have, that’s the kind of thing that makes investors afraid that CoreWeave is going to borrow even moreTo make things worse for CoreWeave, Brannin McBee, one of the company’s cofounders, told the Financial Times — also last week, on the same day as Palihapitiya’s post — that the company wants to have its debt be investment-grade, rather than junk, so that it can borrow from insurers, as their capital is, in his words, “unlimited.” This is not entirely unreasonable — earlier this year, CoreWeave secured its first investment-grade chip loan. But when you talk about wanting to tap into the enormous sums of money that insurers have, that’s the kind of thing that makes investors afraid that CoreWeave — already a massive debtor — is going to borrow even more.“The problem is not that credit profiles have changed in the last year, it’s that we’ve got another year and a half of supply coming,” Bloomberg quoted John Yovanovic, co-head of leveraged finance at MetLife Investment Management, as saying.I have seen people suggest that this means the AI bubble is bursting. I am not so sure. A plunging stock price is not necessarily financial doom. Stocks are an expression of confidence in a company’s future, not a reflection of day-to-day business. But CoreWeave has a lot of very expensive debt, and if that debt gets more expensive, that makes it even harder for CoreWeave to turn a profit.CoreWeave is the poster child for AI debt, and as of its second quarter earnings, owed more than $35 billion. That’s partly because it pioneered GPUs as collateral for loans, and partly because CoreWeave doesn’t have a real business beyond selling compute, a business on which it does not make money — the company lost more than a billion dollars in the first half of the year.The anxieties investors have around CoreWeave are, in fact, present for all neocloudsSo why am I not ready to do a victory lap on this? After all, I have suggested that this business is long-term unsustainable. The answer is “remaining performance obligations” from its customers — $103.7 billion of them as of the second quarter. About 40 percent of that money is due to CoreWeave in 2028, and the companies who’ve agreed to these contracts can’t cancel them except under some very limited circumstances. Its biggest customers are Microsoft, OpenAI, and what is probably Nvidia, though CoreWeave doesn’t disclose who its third-biggest customer is. Those three generated almost three-quarters of the company’s second quarter revenue.Microsoft and Nvidia are probably good for the money — at least, as long as it benefits them to be good for the money. (I suspect they realize that if CoreWeave goes belly-up, there will be plenty of collateral damage in the market, so they are unlikely to push the company over the edge themselves.) OpenAI is shakier, but unless OpenAI is in significantly more financial distress than we all realize, CoreWeave is probably fine for a while. As long as it can continue to pay off its debt, the music keeps going. Only when the AI boom falters are we going to find out if it’s actually a viable business.Still, the angst around CoreWeave has made things shaky for other companies that have taken out significant debt in the AI buildout — Oracle’s shares, for instance, which have fallen almost 10 percent in the same timeframe. There’s been a sell-off in Oracle bonds, too. The anxieties investors have around CoreWeave are, in fact, present for all neoclouds. It’s just not clear the bare-metal business is a good one.Anyway, some people are buying the dip.

history.titleZh: CoreWeave 的债务正成为整个人工智能行业的问题
history.descriptionZh:
CoreWeave上周经历了一个糟糕的星期。其债券按常见标准跌入“困境区间”，即投资者要求的收益率比政府债券高出1000个基点。上周二，被称为“SPAC之王”的Chamath Palihapitiya注意到其困境债务，并公开质疑AI基础设施建设是否正在形成私募信贷泡沫。自上周二收盘以来，CoreWeave股价已下跌超过20%，跌幅相当显著，市场上其他AI公司似乎也受到一定牵连。

文章作者表示，自己此前也质疑过AI行业是否存在泡沫，但当“SPAC之王”开始附和一位长期追问“我们到底打算怎么负担这一切”的人士的担忧时，这释放出的信号完全不同。换句话说，当作者说“情况不妙”是一种分量，当马斯克这样说则是另一种分量。

更令CoreWeave承压的是，公司联合创始人Brannin McBee上周在接受《金融时报》采访时、也就是Palihapitiya发帖同一天表示，CoreWeave希望其债务达到投资级而非垃圾级，从而能够向保险公司借款，因为在他看来保险公司的资金“无限”。这一想法并非完全没有道理：今年早些时候，CoreWeave获得了首笔投资级芯片贷款。但当公司谈论要动用保险公司的巨额资金时，投资者会担心，已经负债累累的CoreWeave将进一步举债。彭博社援引MetLife Investment Management杠杆融资联席主管John Yovanovic的话称，问题不在于过去一年信用状况发生变化，而在于未来一年半还有更多供应涌入。

有人据此认为AI泡沫正在破裂，但作者并不完全认同。股价暴跌不一定意味着财务末日；股票反映的是市场对公司未来的信心，而不是日常经营状况。但CoreWeave确实背负大量昂贵债务，如果债务成本进一步上升，其盈利难度会更大。CoreWeave是AI债务的典型代表，截至第二季度财报，公司负债超过350亿美元。这部分是因为它开创了以GPU作为贷款抵押品的融资模式，部分是因为CoreWeave除了出售算力之外并没有真正成型的业务，而这项业务并不赚钱——公司今年上半年亏损超过10亿美元。

不过，作者并不准备就此宣告CoreWeave失败。关键在于其客户的“剩余履约义务”：截至第二季度达1037亿美元，其中约40%将在2028年到期，签署合同的公司除极少数情况外不能取消。CoreWeave最大客户是微软、OpenAI，以及很可能是英伟达的第三大未披露客户；这三家客户贡献了公司第二季度近四分之三的收入。微软和英伟达大概率具备付款能力，至少在有利益的情况下如此；作者怀疑它们也意识到，如果CoreWeave破产，市场将遭受连带冲击，因此不太可能主动把公司推下悬崖。OpenAI的财务稳定性更弱，但除非其困境远比外界所知严重，否则CoreWeave短期内可能无虞。只要CoreWeave能继续偿还债务，音乐就会继续播放；只有AI繁荣放缓时，才能真正检验其商业模式是否可行。

尽管如此，围绕CoreWeave的焦虑已让其他在AI建设中背负大量债务的公司感到不稳。例如，甲骨文股价在同一时间段下跌近10%，其债券也出现抛售。投资者对CoreWeave的担忧实际上存在于所有“neocloud”公司之中；目前尚不清楚这种裸金属算力租赁业务是否是一门好生意。不过，仍有一些投资者在逢低买入。
